title: Auto-Termination & Warm Pool Cluster Sizing
summary: Set cluster autosuspend to 10-15 minutes for interactive workloads and use serverless SQL warehouses with instant scaling policies.
code: ALTER WAREHOUSE dbsql_wh SET AUTO_SUSPEND = 600 MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT = 1 MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT = 4;

title: Delta Deletion Vectors vs Full File Compaction
summary: Enable Deletion Vectors on high-churn Delta tables to avoid rewriting 500MB Parquet files on single-row updates.

title: Fabric Capacity (F-SKU) Auto-Pause via Azure Logic Apps
summary: Pause non-production Fabric capacities outside business hours (7 PM to 7 AM and weekends) using Azure Logic Apps or CLI, reducing monthly runtime from 730 hours to 220 hours.
code: az fabric capacity suspend --resource-group rg-fabric-dev --capacity-name capfabricdev01

title: Synapse Serverless filepath() & filename() Partition Pruning
summary: Filter directly on directory structure metadata via filepath(1) and filepath(2) to prevent Serverless SQL from scanning unwanted historical year/month Parquet partitions.
code: SELECT r.filepath(1) AS [Year], SUM(r.Total) FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'sales/year=*/month=*/*.parquet', FORMAT='PARQUET') AS r WHERE r.filepath(1) = '2024' GROUP BY r.filepath(1);

title: Automated Storage Lifecycle Tiering: Hot to Cool to Cold to Archive
summary: Configure Azure Storage lifecycle rules to transition Bronze raw landing data from Hot ($0.018/GB) to Cool ($0.010/GB) at 30 days, Cold ($0.0036/GB) at 90 days, and Archive ($0.00099/GB) at 365 days.
code: az storage account management-policy create --account-name mylakehouse --policy @lifecycle_policy.json

title: Parquet Zstandard (ZSTD Level 7) Recompression in Lakehouse
savings: 38% Storage & Read I/O Reduction over Snappy
summary: Re-encode cold and curated Silver/Gold Parquet partitions using ZSTD level 7 compression, cutting disk footprint by 38% with zero perceptible query decompression latency penalty.

title: Cosmos DB Synthetic Partitioning & Targeted Path Indexing
summary: Exclude high-cardinality nested JSON attributes from automatic indexing and append synthetic hash suffixes to partition keys to avoid 10,000 RU/s physical partition throttling.
code: az cosmosdb sql container update --account-name mycosmos --indexing-policy '{"indexingMode":"consistent","includedPaths":[{"path":"/tenantId/?"}],"excludedPaths":[{"path":"/*"}]}'

title: Delta Lake & Iceberg VACUUM Snapshot Compaction
summary: Run regular OPTIMIZE to compact small delta files into 128MB-512MB columnar files and VACUUM to purge historical snapshots older than 7 days, stopping dead storage accumulation.
code:
OPTIMIZE gold.fact_transactions ZORDER BY (customer_id, transaction_date);
VACUUM gold.fact_transactions RETAIN 168 HOURS;

title: Snowflake Query Acceleration Service (QAS) vs Warehouse Upsizing
savings: 40% - 60% Compute Credit Reduction on Outlier Queries
summary: Instead of permanently upsizing an entire Snowflake warehouse from Medium to 2X-Large to handle occasional outlier scans across billions of unclustered rows, enable Query Acceleration Service (QAS). QAS dynamically leases serverless compute slices exclusively for the scan portion of heavy queries, leaving standard queries running on low-cost small clusters.
code:
-- Enable QAS on analytical warehouse with max scale factor cap
ALTER WAREHOUSE analytics_wh SET 
  ENABLE_QUERY_ACCELERATION = TRUE 
  QUERY_ACCELERATION_MAX_SCALE_FACTOR = 8;

-- Identify queries that benefited from QAS acceleration
SELECT query_id, warehouse_name, query_acceleration_bytes_scanned, query_acceleration_partitions_scanned
FROM snowflake.account_usage.query_acceleration_history
WHERE start_time >= CURRENT_DATE() - 7;

title: Databricks Serverless SQL Photon Scaling & 2-Minute Idle Shutdown
savings: 45% Reduction in Idle Cluster Billing vs Classic Clusters
summary: Classic Databricks VM clusters take 3-5 minutes to start and require minimum 10-15 minute auto-termination to avoid start-up thrashing, wasting hundreds of idle compute hours every month. Serverless SQL warehouses boot in under 5 seconds with native C++ Photon execution and can safely auto-suspend after just 2 minutes of inactivity.
code:
-- Configure Databricks Serverless SQL auto-stop and auto-scaling
-- Managed via Databricks REST API or Terraform:
resource "databricks_sql_endpoint" "serverless_bi" {
  name             = "Serverless BI Warehouse"
  cluster_size     = "Medium"
  auto_stop_mins   = 2
  enable_serverless_compute = true
  min_num_clusters = 1
  max_num_clusters = 5
}

title: BigQuery Editions & Slot Reservations vs On-Demand ($6.25/TB)
savings: 30% - 55% Cost Savings at Scale (>1 PB/month scanned)
summary: At enterprise scale, BigQuery's on-demand model ($6.25 per TB scanned) becomes unpredictable and cost-prohibitive. Switching to BigQuery Enterprise Edition with baseline slot reservations (e.g. 100 slots) plus dynamic auto-scaling caps ensures predictable monthly budgeting while preventing runaway queries from scanning 50TB in seconds.
code:
-- Enforce query byte scan safety caps in BigQuery
-- Prevent accidental full-table scans (> 500GB)
#standardSQL
SET @@dataset_project_id = 'prod_analytics';
-- Run query with maximum bytes billed protection
SELECT customer_id, SUM(order_total)
FROM `prod_analytics.sales.transactions`
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01';
-- Configure via CLI or JDBC: maximum_bytes_billed = 536870912000 (500GB)

title: Fabric Capacity Smoothing & Background Job Throttling Guardrails
savings: Prevents 100% Interactive Reporting Outages & SKU Burst Penalties
summary: Microsoft Fabric capacities (F64, F128) use a 24-hour rolling smoothing algorithm for background jobs (Spark, Data Factory) and 5-minute smoothing for interactive visuals (Power BI Direct Lake). When heavy batch notebooks burst to 400% capacity, Fabric schedules CU debt that throttles interactive dashboards hours later. Scheduling Spark batch jobs during non-peak windows with dedicated capacity reservation isolates executive reporting from background ETL spikes.
code:
-- Fabric Capacity Metrics App Alerting Query
SELECT TimeStamp, CapacityId, OperationName, ItemType,
       TotalCU_s, InteractiveCU_s, BackgroundCU_s, ThrottlingStatus
FROM fabric_monitoring.capacity_metrics
WHERE ThrottlingStatus IN ('InteractiveDelay', 'InteractiveReject')
ORDER BY TimeStamp DESC;

title: Power BI Direct Lake Memory Eviction & Cold Parquet Reloads
savings: 60% Capacity CU Savings & Zero DirectQuery Fallback
summary: When Power BI Direct Lake semantic models exceed SKU memory limits or encounter unsupported DAX expressions (e.g., complex parent-child hierarchies or unoptimized many-to-many relationships), queries silently fall back to DirectQuery mode, which exhausts Fabric Capacity Units (CUs) by firing hundreds of ad-hoc SQL queries against OneLake. Enforcing strict dimensional star schemas, pre-calculating complex measures in Spark/Delta Gold tables, and tuning table framing prevents silent fallback and guarantees pure VertiPaq in-memory performance.
code:
-- Detect Power BI Direct Lake fallback to DirectQuery
SELECT OperationName, ItemName, WorkspaceName, Duration_ms, ExecutionMode
FROM fabric_monitoring.semantic_model_executions
WHERE ExecutionMode = 'DirectQuery' -- Flagged fallback
  AND Timestamp >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '24 HOURS'
ORDER BY Duration_ms DESC;

title: Snowflake Dynamic Tables Target Lag Optimization
summary: Setting all Snowflake Dynamic Tables to TARGET_LAG = '1 minute' forces continuous warehouse wakeups and micro-batch commit overhead even when underlying source data changes infrequently or downstream consumers only refresh daily. Downsampling target lag to '1 hour' or '1 day' on summary marts—or synchronizing refresh triggers to upstream ETL completions via TARGET_LAG = DOWNSTREAM—reduces warehouse runtime from 720 hours/month to under 40 hours/month without impacting SLA.
code:
-- Alter Dynamic Table from high-cost 1-minute lag to downstream synchronization
ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE gold.daily_executive_metrics SET 
  TARGET_LAG = '1 hour', 
  WAREHOUSE = reporting_wh;

-- Inspect compute consumption across Dynamic Tables
SELECT name, target_lag, refresh_trigger, text, last_refresh_duration_seconds
FROM snowflake.account_usage.dynamic_table_refresh_history
WHERE start_time >= CURRENT_DATE - 7
ORDER BY last_refresh_duration_seconds DESC;

title: BigQuery BigLake Multi-Cloud Zero-Copy Federation & Metadata Cache
savings: 85% Egress Cost Reduction & Sub-Second Query Acceleration
summary: Querying petabyte-scale data lakes residing in AWS S3 or Azure ADLS Gen2 from BigQuery traditionally required expensive cross-cloud network transfers and high egress bandwidth charges. BigQuery BigLake establishes a secure, zero-copy connection using BigQuery Omni and federated external tables. Enabling metadata caching on BigLake tables caches Parquet file partition schemas and row group statistics locally in BigQuery, accelerating query planning by 10x and cutting scan fees on unchanged files.
code:
-- Configure BigLake External Table with automated metadata caching
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE `analytics.s3_lake_orders`
WITH CONNECTION `us-east-1.aws_s3_connection`
OPTIONS (
  format = 'PARQUET',
  uris = ['s3://corp-lake-bucket/silver/orders/*.parquet'],
  enable_refresh = TRUE,
  refresh_interval_minutes = 30,
  max_staleness = INTERVAL 1 HOUR
);
